title: Wait for the early CI run before pushing the landing commit
summary: When land replaces the early-pushed head with the landing commit (gh.rs land_pr/replace_early), it first waits up to a bounded time (about 10 minutes) for the early commit's workflow run to complete, so the landing run hits the cached pass. If the wait expires or the early run failed, it pushes as today. Audience: Athena maintainers and anyone watching landing CI time.

defaults_applied.how: New fake-host tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check that push ordering and timing happen in fake-host tests, not that fields exist.
CHANGELOG number must be measured and sourced, otherwise marked pending.
One focused change in the landing path.
Fixes the race by waiting for the cache-producing run, not by shortening the CI.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The landing push the request describes is in gh.rs publish/land_pr via replace_early, not in land.rs, which holds planning and classification; land.rs is listed because the request names it, and likely stays unchanged.

Completion is read from the existing PrHost::ci_runs (CiRunState status == completed) for the early commit. The request's 'fmt, clippy, tests' run is the commit's workflow run, so no new host call is needed; if per-run-name filtering is needed, gh.rs gets a small addition.
Wait and sleep reuse the existing Poll sleep injection, with a new bounded-wait setting defaulting to 10 minutes.

The criterion about the next real landing's time cannot be produced by the producer: it needs a landing that happens after this change. The CHANGELOG will say the measurement is pending, not carry a made-up number.

acceptance_criteria.text: A fake-host test (run with cargo test -p athena-core) shows land_pr, with the early head's CI run still in progress, polling ci_runs on the early commit and pushing the landing commit only after the run reports completed.
A fake-host test shows that when the early run is already completed, the landing push happens at once with no sleep calls.

A test shows that when the run never completes within the bounded wait, the landing commit is still pushed, and that the wait is bounded (default about 10 minutes, injectable so the test needs no real sleeping).

A test shows that a failed (or timed-out) early run, and an early commit with no runs or a ci_runs error, change nothing about merging: land pushes and merges exactly as before and the full landing run decides.
cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets are clean, and cargo fmt --check passes; existing land_pr and publish tests still pass.
The wait applies only when an early head exists and differs from the landing commit; the wait is logged or reported in a way a reader can see how long it waited and why it stopped.

CHANGELOG.md has an entry for this change that says the next real landing's time is still to be measured. It must not state an invented number. The measured time is recorded only once a real landing has been observed, with its source (for example the PR number and the run timestamps).

out_of_scope: Changing CI workflows or the early-PR opening order at run.rs:1645
Re-running or fixing failed early runs
Changing merge method or the existing check-wait and re-run logic in wait_for_checks
departures: The CHANGELOG measured landing time depends on a future real landing, which makes verification less likely to pass than the reference. gh.rs is large and the poll/sleep wiring touches many call sites, which raises cost slightly.
urgent_reason: Cuts about 14 minutes of redundant CI (the landing run repeats the early run's full 16 minutes) from every landing, which is wasted time Athena currently repeats.
